headline: Progress is improvement over time—but not all change is progress, and progress isn't automatic
universal_truth: Things can get better; but making them better requires intention, effort, and wisdom about what 'better' means
fun_facts: Global extreme poverty has fallen from 40% to under 10% since 1990
Child mortality has dropped by more than half since 1990
Technology progress is exponential—more computing power in a smartphone than in all of NASA during the moon landing
discussion_questions: What has genuinely improved in your lifetime?
What gets called 'progress' that might not be?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Your ancestors died of diseases we now prevent with vaccines. They worked in conditions we'd consider abuse. They lacked conveniences you take for granted. Things can genuinely get better—progress is real. But not automatic, and not in all dimensions.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We assume things naturally improve, or that all change is progress. But improvement requires effort, and 'better' depends on what you're measuring. What actually constitutes progress?

options.text: Progress is measurable improvement toward valued goals—but what counts as improvement depends on what you value, and it requires intentional effort
options.response: Yes. Progress isn't automatic—it requires defining goals, measuring against them, and working toward them. Different values yield different definitions of progress.

options.text: Progress is when things change for the better over time
options.response: True, but 'better' is the question—better for whom, by what measure...

q1.title: Real Improvements
q1.script: By many measures, life has improved dramatically: longevity, health, literacy, poverty reduction. These gains are real and hard-won. Denying progress ignores genuine achievement and the effort behind it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Real Improvements"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Trade-Offs and Costs
q2.script: Progress in one dimension often costs progress in another. Industrial productivity brought pollution. Digital connection brought distraction. Acknowledging trade-offs doesn't deny progress—it enables wiser progress.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Intentional Improvement
q3.script: Progress isn't natural law—it's human effort. People worked to cure diseases, expand rights, build infrastructure. Believing things can improve, and working to improve them, creates the reality of progress.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Things can get better. But making them better requires intention, effort, and wisdom about what 'better' means. Progress is a project, not a guarantee.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 210—210 days of learning! Tomorrow, we'll explore when everything changes fast—revolution. Until then, identify one area where you want progress and consider what 'better' would mean.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Progress Definition - What's Better?
growTrack.activity: Pick an area of your life where you want progress. Define what 'better' would look like—specifically. What would you measure? What are the trade-offs? Clear definitions of improvement enable intentional progress.
